consequences.power_loss: The null holds size and costs power on the production scores. It stays an opt-in null for data whose stage dispersion is unequal, documented with the cells it loses; predictive_orthonormal is not reopened.
consequences.propose_paper_grade: As within_stage_validated, and a separate change runs predictive_orthonormal under within-stage draws at 500 x 999 with a rank rule for a fixed measured dimension. Only its verdict may change a default.
consequences.reproduction_failed: No reading is interpreted. The cause is fixed and the affected units are rerun under the same rule.
consequences.size_excess: The within-stage null does not hold size in the named family. The option stays an opt-in diagnostic, documented as such; no case study reports it as a test, and predictive_orthonormal is not reopened.
consequences.specificity_excess: The null holds size and reads more off-target rejections than the bound allows. It stays opt-in, documented with those readings; predictive_orthonormal is not reopened.
consequences.within_stage_validated: The within-stage null is a validated opt-in null for the production measurement. A separate change may apply it to the SEA-AD case study and decide the default. predictive_orthonormal stays an opt-in diagnostic for the named reason.

notes: Layer 1 judges the within-stage null on the production scores; layer 2 judges predictive_orthonormal under within-stage draws against production under the same draws, so a gain is the coordinates' and not the null's. Layer 2 bears on the verdict only when layer 1 holds.
A band off-target reading counts against the null only above the size bound and with a paired excess against the unrestricted null, so restored size is not read as a leak.
Every table under 'descriptive' is a reading beside the verdict and never changes it.
